events.title: US September CPI — +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Headline inflation accelerated to 3.7% y/y and core firmed, keeping a December Fed hike on the table despite the October pause.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE on Oct 29 will confirm whether inflation pressure is broadening.

events.title: US September retail sales — +0.8% m/m
events.why_it_matters: The upside surprise was flattered by gasoline; ex-gas growth was only 0.2%, so the consumer picture is weaker than the headline.
events.what_to_watch: September PCE consumption data on Oct 29 for confirmation of the underlying trend.

events.title: China Q3 GDP — 4.5% y/y, beats 4.3% prior
events.why_it_matters: Growth accelerated from Q2 and kept China inside the 4.5–5% annual target, reducing near-term stimulus urgency but supporting global cyclical sentiment.
events.what_to_watch: Fifth Plenum outcome (Oct 26–29) for any shift in the 2027 growth target or policy tone.

events.title: China September industrial production +5.5%, retail sales +1.1%
events.why_it_matters: Production beat but consumption remained soft, reinforcing the two-speed China recovery and the case for targeted rather than broad stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Any consumption-support measures announced after the Plenum.

events.title: China October LPR held at 3.0%/3.5% for 17th month
events.why_it_matters: The PBOC is prioritising bank margins and a policy-rate overhaul over near-term easing, limiting the impulse to property and credit-sensitive sectors.
events.what_to_watch: PBOC liquidity operations and any structural tool tweaks after the Plenum.

events.title: China restricts export of AI and chip-design technologies
events.why_it_matters: Beijing added 23 AI technologies to its export-control list and imposed registration on outbound frontier models and chip IP, escalating tech fragmentation.
events.what_to_watch: US and allied response; potential impact on Nvidia and semiconductor supply chains.

events.title: Taiwan tightens AI chip and server export controls to China
events.why_it_matters: Taipei moved to criminalise unauthorised AI chip and server exports to China, aligning with US restrictions and adding compliance cost to the semiconductor supply chain.
events.what_to_watch: Enforcement actions and any retaliation from Beijing.

events.title: Supreme Court IEEPA tariff refunds — CIT certifies importer class
events.why_it_matters: The CIT class certification opens a clearer path for importers to recover IEEPA tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court, a cash-flow positive for retailers but a fiscal negative.
events.what_to_watch: Refund timeline and whether the administration appeals or introduces replacement tariffs.

events.title: Trump delays wind turbine tariffs for 180 days
events.why_it_matters: The executive order avoids immediate national-security tariffs on turbines already subject to steel, aluminium and copper duties, easing near-term cost pressure on renewables developers.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the tariff reprieve is extended beyond 180 days.

events.title: US sanctions escalate on Russia and Iran energy networks
events.why_it_matters: OFAC targeted Iranian banks and shadow-fleet facilitators while the Graham sanctions act authorises secondary tariffs on buyers of Russian energy, keeping oil supply risk elevated.
events.what_to_watch: Iranian retaliation and whether secondary sanctions deter Chinese and Indian buyers.

events.title: Meta Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AI ad monetisation and 2027 capex guidance set the tone for the mega-cap AI trade just before Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report.
events.what_to_watch: Capex guidance from the mega-cap cohort reporting this week.

events.title: Tesla Q3 2026 earnings — profit down 42.7%, beat on EPS
events.why_it_matters: Tesla beat depressed estimates and turned free cash flow positive, but margins and EV demand remain the sector bellwether into year-end.
events.what_to_watch: October delivery data and margin trajectory in Q4.

events.title: Netflix Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Ad-tier engagement and pricing trends set the tone for streaming margins and the media complex into year-end.
events.what_to_watch: Ad-tier subscriber growth and any further price increases.

events.title: France riots and political crisis after cost-of-living protests
events.why_it_matters: France suffered its worst unrest in years, weakening the government and reinforcing the case for the ECB to hold rather than hike on October 29.
events.what_to_watch: French OAT-Bund spread and whether unrest spreads to other EU countries.

events.title: Japan September core CPI rises to 2.1%, core-core 2.4%
events.why_it_matters: Core inflation exceeded 2% for the first time in nine months, strengthening the case for a December BOJ hike even as the October 30 meeting is expected to hold.
events.what_to_watch: BOJ October 30 outlook report and Ueda's guidance on December.

events.title: Eurozone October flash PMI misses — services 51.7 vs 52.5 expected
events.why_it_matters: Growth momentum slowed in October while input prices accelerated on energy, leaving the ECB caught between a weak economy and 3.8% inflation.
events.what_to_watch: ECB October 29 decision and Lagarde's signal on December.

events.title: Brent crude above $111 on Strait of Hormuz attacks
events.why_it_matters: The US-Israel-Iran conflict continues to disrupt oil flows and shipping through Hormuz, keeping a geopolitical risk premium in crude and global inflation expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Any escalation before the US midterms and the OPEC+ November 1 meeting.

events.title: Brazil presidential runoff — Lula wins, Bolsonaro contests
events.why_it_matters: Lula's narrow victory removes immediate election uncertainty but the contested result raises the risk of political instability in Latin America's largest economy.
events.what_to_watch: Legal challenges from Flavio Bolsonaro and market reaction to the result.

events.title: Trump lifts some Canada tariffs, adds new ones ahead of midterms
events.why_it_matters: The executive order removes 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products from Oct 30 but adds tariffs on dozens of other goods, a pre-election political calculation with limited net trade impact.
events.what_to_watch: Canadian retaliation and whether the change affects specific sectors like lumber or food.

events.title: South Korea semiconductor exports surge 222.5% in first 20 days of October
events.why_it_matters: AI-driven chip demand is driving record Korean exports, confirming the semiconductor upcycle remains strong despite China's export restrictions.
events.what_to_watch: Full-month October trade data and Samsung/SK Hynix guidance.

events.title: China Fifth Plenum opens — 2027 growth targets in focus
events.why_it_matters: The Plenum will finalise 2027 economic targets and signal the policy mix for the next year, with markets watching for any shift toward stronger consumption support or continued quality-over-quantity restraint.
events.what_to_watch: Communique on Oct 29 for growth target language and any new stimulus measures.

events.title: Anthropic IPO — S-1 filing expected as early as today
events.why_it_matters: A public filing for a potential $100bn raise and $2trn valuation would be the largest tech IPO ever, testing market appetite for AI mega-caps amid a choppy tech tape.
events.what_to_watch: Timing of the S-1 and initial valuation range; roadshow expected Nov 9.

events.title: FOMC meeting — hold expected at 3.75–4.00%
events.why_it_matters: Markets price ~90% probability of a hold, but the statement and Powell's tone will be scrutinised for signals on a December hike given sticky inflation and firm growth.
events.what_to_watch: Powell's press conference and any dissent in the vote; December hike pricing.

events.title: US Q3 GDP advance and September PCE
events.why_it_matters: Consensus expects Q3 GDP at 3.2% annualised and core PCE at 2.4% q/q; a hot core PCE would cement a December hike, while a growth miss would complicate the Fed's path.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE y/y (expected 3.1%) and any revisions to prior quarters.

events.title: ECB meeting — hold expected, December signal in focus
events.why_it_matters: The ECB is expected to hold at 2.50%, but Lagarde may signal a December hike if energy-driven inflation persists, while French political turmoil complicates the outlook.
events.what_to_watch: Lagarde's language on energy pass-through and the French OAT spread.

events.title: Bank of Japan meeting — hold expected at 1.25%
events.why_it_matters: The BOJ is expected to hold but may revise up its 2027 inflation forecast, keeping a December hike on the table and supporting yen volatility.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's press conference and the quarterly outlook report.

events.title: Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon earnings
events.why_it_matters: About 36% of the S&P 500 reports this week; AI capex, cloud growth and ad spending will determine whether the mega-cap tech rally can resume after a soft patch.
events.what_to_watch: Azure and AWS growth rates, AI capex guidance, and Alphabet's cloud margin.

events.title: Apple Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Apple closes the mega-cap earnings series; iPhone demand, China revenue and services growth will be key for the consumer tech narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Greater China revenue and any commentary on AI features.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.why_it_matters: Prediction markets price high odds of a Democratic sweep, which could constrain corporate tax cuts and increase regulation in tech and AI; markets may see a 'sell the rumor, buy the news' pattern.
events.what_to_watch: Senate and House control, and the market reaction on Nov 4.

events.title: OPEC+ November 1 meeting
events.why_it_matters: The group will review production after holding November quotas; with Brent above $111, any signal of a supply increase could ease prices, while a rollover would keep the risk premium elevated.
events.what_to_watch: Saudi and Russian stance on output and compliance from Iraq/Kazakhstan.

events.title: Anthropic IPO roadshow and potential listing
events.why_it_matters: If completed, the IPO could set a new valuation benchmark for AI companies and absorb significant market liquidity, but timing is conditional on market conditions.
events.what_to_watch: Roadshow demand and whether the listing slips to 2027.

events.title: US October jobs report
events.why_it_matters: The last major labour-market print before the December FOMC; a strong report would reinforce the case for a hike, while a weak print would shift the debate toward growth risks.
events.what_to_watch: Nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate and average hourly earnings.

events.title: SEMICON West 2026
events.why_it_matters: The conference highlighted the industry's path to a $1 trillion milestone and showcased AI-driven demand, supporting the semiconductor capex narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through orders for equipment makers and any China-related export control commentary.

events.title: OPEC+ holds November production steady
events.why_it_matters: The decision to maintain September quotas for November kept supply tight as US-Iran tensions disrupted flows, supporting elevated oil prices.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance and the next meeting on Nov 1.

events.title: US new home sales and durable goods orders
events.why_it_matters: New home sales and durable goods provide an early read on interest-rate-sensitive demand and business investment ahead of the GDP and Fed decision.
events.what_to_watch: Durable goods ex-transport and any weather-related distortion in housing.

top_risks: FOMC hawkish hold and hot core PCE (Oct 29) could revive December hike pricing, pressuring long-duration tech and rate-sensitive sectors.
US midterm election outcome (Nov 3) — a Democratic sweep could trigger regulatory and tax policy uncertainty, leading to a pre-election risk-off move.
Escalation of US-Iran/Israel conflict before the midterms could spike oil above $120 and disrupt global shipping, feeding inflation and hitting consumer spending.
China's Fifth Plenum may disappoint on stimulus, leaving global cyclicals and commodity exporters exposed to slower Chinese demand.
Anthropic's mega-IPO could absorb market liquidity and test AI valuation resilience, especially if the tech tape remains fragile.
top_opportunities: Mega-cap tech earnings (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Apple) could re-ignite the AI trade if cloud growth and capex guidance beat expectations.
A benign Fed hold combined with soft GDP could spark a relief rally in rate-sensitive growth stocks and small caps.
South Korea's semiconductor export boom signals continued strength in the AI chip cycle, benefiting equipment makers and memory suppliers.
OPEC+ supply discipline and geopolitical risk premium support energy stocks and oil-linked currencies.
Any China stimulus surprise after the Plenum could lift Basic Materials, Industrials, and emerging-market equities.
summary: Markets enter the final week of October with a Fed hold largely priced, sticky inflation, Brent above $111 on Hormuz risk, and a pivotal mega-cap earnings week. The FOMC, Q3 GDP/core PCE, the US midterms and a possible post-election Iran escalation dominate the next two weeks, while China's Fifth Plenum and Anthropic's IPO add policy and liquidity risk. The main tension is between a market pricing a benign Fed pause and a data-dependent path that could force a December hike.
